guide.title: New London, Connecticut: The Whaling City's Harbor
guide.intro: New London was founded in 1646 by John Winthrop Jr., who named it and its river — the Thames — after England's capital. Incorporated in 1784 as one of Connecticut's first five cities, it served as the colony's first official port and, by the nineteenth century, ranked as New England's second-largest whaling and sealing port by volume, earning the nickname "The Whaling City." The city's history includes hard blows: on September 6, 1781, British forces under the turncoat Benedict Arnold attacked Forts Trumbull and Griswold and burned the town. The schooner Amistad entered New London harbor in late August 1839, an event now commemorated inside the 1833 U.S. Custom House on Bank Street. Playwright Eugene O'Neill spent boyhood summers here at Monte Cristo Cottage. Today the U.S. Coast Guard Academy, Fort Trumbull, and Ocean Beach define a city still built around its harbor.

sections.heading: The Whaling City's harbor
sections.body: New London was founded in 1646 by John Winthrop Jr., who named it and its river — the Thames — after England's capital. Incorporated in 1784 as one of Connecticut's first five cities, it served as the colony's first official port and, by the nineteenth century, ranked as New England's second-largest whaling and sealing port by volume, earning the nickname "The Whaling City." The city's history includes hard blows: on September 6, 1781, British forces under the turncoat Benedict Arnold attacked Forts Trumbull and Griswold and burned the town. The schooner Amistad entered New London harbor in late August 1839, an event now commemorated inside the 1833 U.S. Custom House on Bank Street — designed by architect Robert Mills and a museum since 1983. Playwright Eugene O'Neill spent boyhood summers here at Monte Cristo Cottage, preserved today by the Eugene O'Neill Theater Center.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Drivers reach New London directly off I-95, with CT Routes 32 and 85 feeding the city. Train travelers arrive at the 1887 H.H. Richardson-designed Union Station (27-35 Water Street), served by about nine Amtrak Northeast Regional trains each direction daily (Acela no longer stops here) and by CTrail Shore Line East commuter trains from New Haven. Cross Sound Ferry connections to Long Island, Fishers Island, and Block Island depart steps from the station.

sections.heading: Forts, museums, and the harborfront
sections.body: Fort Trumbull State Park, built 1839-1852 on a site first fortified in 1777, spans more than 225 years of military history on the harbor. The Lyman Allyn Art Museum, founded in 1932, and the Garde Arts Center, a 1926 downtown theater, anchor the arts scene, while Ocean Beach Park offers a city-owned boardwalk on Long Island Sound. Verified lodging inside New London's city limits was sparse when this guide was researched — Groton and Mystic to the east offer verified hotel options.

faq.question: How do I get to New London?
faq.answer: Drivers use I-95 with CT Routes 32 and 85 feeding downtown. By rail, Union Station (27-35 Water Street) has about nine Amtrak Northeast Regional trains each direction daily (Acela no longer stops) plus CTrail Shore Line East service from New Haven; Cross Sound Ferry connections depart nearby.

faq.question: Can I take the train from New London to New York?
faq.answer: Yes — Amtrak Northeast Regional runs about nine trains each direction daily from Union Station toward New York on the Northeast Corridor. Acela no longer stops at New London.

faq.question: Why is New London called 'The Whaling City'?
faq.answer: By volume, New London was New England's second-largest whaling and sealing port in the nineteenth century, a legacy that gave the city its nickname.

faq.question: What happened to New London during the Revolutionary War?
faq.answer: On September 6, 1781, British forces commanded by the turncoat Benedict Arnold attacked Forts Trumbull and Griswold and burned the city — the same raid remembered in Groton at Fort Griswold Battlefield State Park.

faq.question: What is the Custom House Maritime Museum?
faq.answer: Housed in the 1833 U.S. Custom House on Bank Street, designed by architect Robert Mills, it has been a museum since 1983 and includes a permanent exhibition on the schooner Amistad's 1839 arrival in New London harbor. Open Thursday-Sunday, 1-5 p.m. (Saturday from 10 a.m.).

faq.question: Where can I stay in New London?
faq.answer: Verified lodging directly in New London was limited when this guide was researched; travelers should check current chain listings directly, or consider Groton or Mystic to the east.

places.name: Fort Trumbull State Park
places.summary: The current fort was built 1839-1852 on a site first fortified in 1777 to guard New London Harbor; the original fort was destroyed in Benedict Arnold's 1781 raid. Grounds open daily 8 a.m.-sunset, free; visitor center/fort Wed-Sun 9-5 Memorial Day-Labor Day, adult tickets $6.
places.history: The site spans over 225 years of military history from the Revolution to the Cold War.

places.name: Lyman Allyn Art Museum
places.summary: Founded in 1932, the museum is known for strong collections of American paintings and decorative arts. Open Tuesday-Saturday 10-5, Sunday 1-5.

places.name: Garde Arts Center
places.summary: A downtown theater that opened in 1926, celebrating its centennial in 2026. Box office hours Tuesday-Friday 10-5.

places.name: Custom House Maritime Museum
places.summary: Housed in the 1833 U.S. Custom House designed by architect Robert Mills, a museum since 1983, with a permanent exhibition on the schooner Amistad's arrival in New London harbor in late August 1839. Open Thursday-Sunday 1-5 (Saturday from 10), $10 adults, free for New London residents.

places.name: Captain Scott's Lobster Dock
places.summary: A family-owned waterfront seafood shack on Shaw's Cove, famous for lobster rolls, operating since 1996 and celebrating 30 years in 2026. Open daily 11 a.m.-8 p.m.

places.name: Fred's Shanty
places.summary: A Pequot Avenue seafood-and-ice-cream stand and local institution since 1972, serving fried seafood, pizza, subs, and Hershey's ice cream. Daily hours 11 a.m.-8/9 p.m.

places.name: On the Waterfront
places.summary: A seafood and Italian restaurant with harbor views, run by Stash Schiavone and Chef Anthony Schiavone.
